[page[title]]

Production code must not contain non-documentation comments.

What The Standard says

“Abstraction” — The Standard's production examples rely on explicit types, operations and extracted methods to express intent. The analyser favors that self-describing implementation over narrative comments that can become stale. read it here.
“internal details” — The Standard protects maintainability by keeping implementation details controlled and refactorable. Documentation comments remain valid API documentation, while implementation commentary should be expressed through clearer code. read it here.

Why it matters

Production code should communicate intent through names, structure, and documentation contracts rather than narrating implementation with incidental comments. Removing non-documentation comments prevents stale explanations from contradicting behaviour and exposes code that needs clearer design.

Bad code example

// Violates STXFORMAT010: Production code must not contain non-documentation comments.
// Submit the student.
Submit(student);

Good code example

// Follows STXFORMAT010
/// <summary>Submits an student.</summary>
ValueTask SubmitStudent(Student student) => default;
